pageCache.pageTitle: Little Horsted Church of England Primary School - Attendance
pageCache.text:
Attendance
Did you know that across the year there are just 190 school days? That means there are already 175 days set aside for weekends, holidays, family visits and rewarding days out. We believe every school day counts to give your child the greatest opportunity of attaining a good education and to support a happy and healthy future. We will always seek to work with parents to support their child's attendance at school and look to remove barriers to regular attendance.
Parents can view their child's attendance at any point on Arbor.
Guidance and resources for attendance can be found at:
Resources for families | Children's Commissioner for England
Working together to improve school attendance
Attendance & Leave of Absence Request Form
Please note that copies of this form can be collected from the school office.Withdrawal from Learning Application
Illness
The NHS and the Chief Medical Officer say it is usually appropriate for parents and carers to send their children to school with mild respiratory illnesses, including general cold symptoms like a minor cough, runny nose or sore throat. Please refer to the following link for further information
Is my child too ill for school? - NHS
If your child is ill, please inform the school by telephone 01825 750380 or email office@littlehorsted.e-sussex.sch.uk on the first day of absence.

pageCache.pageTitle: Little Horsted Church of England Primary School - Modern Foreign Languages
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages
Modern Foreign Languages (MFL) INTENT statement
At Little Horsted CE Primary School, our MFL is French. The curriculum in Key Stage 2 is guided by our vision to Live, Love, Learn in the Light of the Lord and shaped by the values of kindness, love, respect, aspiration, resilience and community.
We follow the Language Angels scheme to provide a structured, engaging and progressive approach to learning French, enabling children to develop strong foundations in listening, speaking, reading and writing. Through interactive lessons, songs, games and meaningful vocabulary work, pupils build confidence and aspiration as language learners, developing the resilience needed to practise, make mistakes and improve. Our teaching promotes respect for other cultures and languages, nurturing curiosity about the wider world and reinforcing a sense of global community. Children learn to communicate with kindness and appreciation for diversity, recognising that language learning helps deepen understanding of others.
Our intent is for every pupil to leave Key Stage 2 with a positive attitude toward languages, a growing linguistic toolkit, and the confidence to continue their language learning journey as they Live, Love and Learn in the Light of the Lord.
French curriculum overview
‘A high-quality languages education should foster pupils’ curiosity and deepen their understanding of the world. The teaching should enable pupils to express their ideas and thoughts in another language and to understand and respond to its speakers, both in speech and in writing.’ (National Curriculum 2014 – Appendix A

pageCache.pageTitle: Little Horsted Church of England Primary School - Music
pageCache.text:
Music
Music INTENT statement
Music Lessons and Performances
At Little Horsted, music is woven into the fabric of school life. Through our Sing Up scheme, every child takes part in a dedicated weekly music lesson of up to 50 minutes. Each session includes vocal and physical warm-ups, a main musical activity, and a chance to share learning through performance.
Singing is central to our school community. Children enjoy singing together in Collective Worship and at church services, enriching both our worship and our celebrations.
In the academic year 2025/26, we are following Year B of the scheme.
Learning an Instrument
For those children wanting to learn a specific instrument are able to provide opportunites for the following:
Details of how to apply can be found at the school office.Primary National Curriculum - Music

pageCache.pageTitle: Little Horsted Church of England Primary School - Reading
pageCache.text:
Reading
Reading INTENT statement
At Little Horsted CE Primary School, we believe that reading opens doors to imagination, understanding and lifelong learning. We want every child to see themselves as a reader and to develop a genuine love of books that will stay with them throughout their lives. Through high-quality texts, rich discussions and meaningful reading experiences, we nurture confident, fluent readers who are curious about the world around them. Rooted in our Christian values, we encourage children to read with empathy, wonder and enjoyment, helping them to grow not only as successful learners but also as thoughtful, compassionate individuals. Our aim is for every child to leave Little Horsted with the skills, confidence and enthusiasm to read for both purpose and pleasure.
Useful resources

pageCache.pageTitle: Little Horsted Church of England Primary School - Science
pageCache.text:
Science
Science INTENT statement
At Little Horsted CE Primary School, our Science curriculum is rooted in our vision to Live, Love, Learn in the Light of the Lord, encouraging children to explore God’s world with curiosity, wonder and responsibility. We believe hands‑on investigation is vital, and we give pupils rich opportunities to develop their scientific thinking and knowledge through practical experiments and enquiry questions linked, where meaningful, to our termly themes.
Our values shape the way Science is taught: kindness and love are shown through collaborative investigations and respect for living things; respect guides thoughtful discussion and careful use of equipment; community is strengthened as children work together to test ideas and share discoveries; aspiration inspires pupils to pursue new questions and tackle challenging concepts; and resilience is built as they repeat tests, refine predictions and learn from unexpected results.
Through this values‑driven approach, we aim to develop confident young scientists who can ask meaningful questions, plan fair tests, analyse findings and feel excited by the discoveries they make, enabling them to thrive in a rapidly changing world as they Live, Love and Learn in the Light of the Lord.

pageCache.pageTitle: Little Horsted Church of England Primary School - Sports Premium
pageCache.text:
Sports Premium
PE and Sport Premium at Little Horsted CE Primary School
The PE and Sport Premium is a government grant provided to primary schools in England to help improve the quality of physical education (PE), sport, and physical activity for all pupils.
The aim is to ensure that children:
Engage in at least 60 minutes of physical activity each day (20 minutes for disabled children)
Have access to high-quality PE lessons and a wide range of sports
Develop healthy, active lifestyles from an early age
You can find out more about it here: PE and sport premium for primary schools - GOV.UK
Please see below for our report regarding the use of the PE and Sports Premium at our school
PE and Sport Premium Report 2024-25

pageCache.pageTitle: Little Horsted Church of England Primary School - Our Curriculum Intent
pageCache.text:
Our Curriculum Intent
The Curriculum at Little Horsted CE Primary School
Curriculum Intent
At Little Horsted CE Primary, our curriculum grows from our Christian vision: Live, Love, Learn in the Light of the Lord. We believe every child is unique, and we aim to nurture the whole child so they flourish academically, socially and spiritually.
As a small rural school, we create a warm, caring environment where relationships are strong and every child is known and valued.
Our curriculum follows the Early Years Foundation Stage and National Curriculum, but is enriched with experiences that spark curiosity, kindness, creativity, and resilience.
We offer a broad, engaging curriculum that encourages children to explore, think deeply and develop confidence in who they are. Through vibrant, hands‑on learning, we support each child to grow their talents, develop a love of learning, and feel ready for the next stage of their journey as they Live, Love, Learn in the Light of the Lord.
Key Principles
At Little Horsted, we believe that every child is precious, unique, and held in God’s light. We aim to guide our children so that they:
Above all, we want each child to know they are loved, to discover who they are called to be, and to grow into people who use their light to make a positive difference in God’s world.
Curriculum
Our curriculum follows learning journeys in each class, taking into account our geographical location, the local farming community and the rich historical heritage of the area as well as meeting all the National Curriculum requirements.
We follow the National Curriculum programmes of study in Years 1-6 and in the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) we use the EYFS framework and Development Matters documents.
Please see the subject pages to the right for more information about each subject.
Class pages have further details about the areas we study in each term as well as the curriculum coverage for each year group.

pageCache.pageTitle: Little Horsted Church of England Primary School - Computing
pageCache.text:
Computing
Computing Intent statement
At Little Horsted CE Primary School, our Computing curriculum is guided by our vision to Live, Love, Learn in the Light of the Lord, equipping children with the skills, knowledge and confidence they need to thrive in an ever‑evolving digital world.
Through a carefully sequenced progression of learning using Teach Computing, pupils develop secure understanding of computing systems, networks, programming, digital media and data handling, growing as both imaginative creators and logical problem‑solvers.
Our school values shape the way Computing is taught: kindness and love are shown as children collaborate, support one another and communicate respectfully online; respect underpins safe, responsible digital behaviour and thoughtful use of technology; community is strengthened as pupils work together on shared projects and use technology to connect learning across the curriculum; aspiration encourages them to design increasingly complex programs and digital content; and resilience is fostered as they debug code, refine ideas and persevere through challenges. Through meaningful, real‑world tasks - such as creating animations, building 3D models or designing quizzes - children learn to use technology confidently as both consumers and creators, developing the digital literacy needed to live, love and learn in the Light of the Lord as responsible, innovative citizens of the future.
